sections.name: Team Cluster 01
sections.description: A team section built around the avatar cluster — copy and a live detail panel on one side, a hatched grid of faces on the other. Hovering or selecting a face pops a role badge beside it and rewrites the panel; phones drop the cluster for a real list.

variations.name: default
variations.description: A team section built around the avatar cluster. Perfet to use to showcase your team details in a website.

props.name: members
props.description: The team. Extends the avatar block's AvatarMember with optional `bio` and `links`. Defaults to a six-person studio.

props.name: members[].icon
props.description: HugeIcons icon shown at the leading edge of that person's row. Optional and unset by default for custom members — six copies of one generic user glyph is decoration, so a row with nothing specific to show renders without one.

props.name: members[].bio
props.description: One short phrase shown under the name in the role row, ~40 characters. It is clamped to a single line so the list stays about as tall as the square cluster beside it.

props.name: members[].links
props.description: Links rendered under the bio for the active member.

props.name: eyebrow
props.description: Small label above the heading, uppercased and letterspaced in CSS — pass it in natural case. Defaults to "Know my team".

props.name: heading
props.description: Section heading. Defaults to "The people behind the work".

props.name: body
props.description: Paragraph under the heading.

props.name: className
props.description: Additional classes on the section element.

variations.previewHint: Pick a row under the copy or a face on the right — either one drives the other
features: Ships its own namespaced colour tokens, each defined as the theme token with a literal fallback, so the section inherits a host theme where one exists and stands alone where none does — and never overwrites the consumer's base tokens
Colour comes from the theme's semantic tokens rather than hardcoded neutrals, so the section themes with the app it is installed into

Each row leads with an icon chosen for that specific role — a compass, a paint board, a source-code mark — rather than one generic glyph repeated six times, which would be decoration; it also gives the row the affordance plain text never had
Row icons are `currentColor` at 1.5px stroke, so they inherit the row's active colour with no second asset and carry the same optical weight as the 14px label beside them
Row name and description sit on `foreground/70` and `muted-foreground` rather than neutral-400/600, which measured ~2.6:1 on white and ~2.3:1 on near-black — under WCAG AA for text that small

The cluster stays a presentation block and reports its active member outward through `onActiveChange`, so the section owns layout and copy while the block keeps owning the grid — no fork, one implementation

One cluster at every width — same 5×5, same cells, same arrangement, only the tile size changing — so the phone and the desktop show the same picture rather than two layouts that have to be learned separately
The grid's gutter steps down on small screens, which is the one place a phone can win pixels per tile back without altering the layout
Below 1280 the badge is the only detail surface, so `renderBadge` puts name and role in the pill; at 1280 and up the badge is hidden and the copy list takes over
The role pills and the cluster are two views of one state, not two components kept in sync — the grid runs controlled, so picking a role and clicking a face are literally the same write

Each row runs role left, name right, justified apart and divided by the same 45° hatch at the same 6px pitch as the placeholder shells — a heavier ink, because a 4px band needs it to read — which ties the two halves together without repeating the dashed outline
Row descriptions are clamped to one line: at two lines every row grows ~14px, and six of those made the copy column visibly taller than the square cluster it sits beside
Hover previews and click commits, so a touch user can select a member at all; the committed selection is what the panel falls back to when the pointer leaves
The detail panel is a single DOM node moved between grid areas by `grid-template-areas`, not two copies shown and hidden — it is aria-live, and a duplicate would announce every change twice

At ≥1280px the role badge moves off the photo and into the panel under the copy: the panel is already in the reading path there, so a badge over the tile would repeat it and cover the face it names. Below 1280 the layout stacks and the panel falls well under the cluster, so the on-tile badge earns its place again
That breakpoint swap is one CSS rule against a `data-role-badge` hook on the block, not a resize listener — no breakpoint state to hydrate, no re-render on resize
Section entrance borrows the cluster's own easing and ring stagger instead of introducing a second timing vocabulary, so heading, faces and panel read as one piece

sections.name: Orchid AI 01
sections.description: A split hero: a plain greige panel with the navbar stamped into its top-left corner as a notch and the type stack bottom-anchored, beside a photographic panel carrying a hub-and-spoke diagram. Three context tiles fan into the Orchid mark, three result cards fan out of it, and pulses travel the outbound connectors only.

variations.name: default
variations.description: A hero section made for OrchidAI.

props.name: className
props.description: Appended to the outer <section> — where a different page background or vertical rhythm goes, since the section ships its own full-bleed padding and min-height.

props.name: imageSrc
props.description: Photograph behind the right panel, passed to next/image with `fill`. OPTIONAL IN TYPE, REQUIRED IN PRACTICE: a registry item carries its files as text inside JSON, so a PNG has no way through, and the default names a file that exists only in the CraftUI repo. Pass your own path, or put a file at `public/paper-image/image01.png`, before shipping. The panel paints no fallback ground, so an unresolved path renders next/image's broken state; pass a real path rather than an empty string, which next/image rejects outright.

props.name: imageAlt
props.description: Alt text for that photograph. Defaults to a description of the lavender-meadow image the hero was composed against, so it has to be replaced whenever `imageSrc` is.

variations.previewHint: Watch the pulses run outward from the mark — narrow the window past md to see the diagram stack
features: The diagram is a flex row — tiles, connectors, hub, connectors, cards — instead of a fixed 560×360 design box scaled by a transform, so every size in it is a Tailwind class that can take a `md:` variant

Connector columns measure their own width and height and solve their elbow paths at runtime; lane centres are 1/6, 3/6 and 5/6 of the measured height, which is exactly where a `grid-rows-3` sibling puts each row's centre, so the paths cannot drift out of alignment with what they connect
Connector radius is clamped against both the horizontal and vertical span, so a narrow column degrades to a gentler curve rather than a self-intersecting one
Below md the row stacks: the tiles become a horizontal strip, the cards go full-width, and the connectors are dropped, since there is no useful diagonal to draw in a 340px column
The navbar is a notch stamped into the panel's corner, not a pill on top of it — one convex round plus two radial-gradient flares make the junctions tangent-continuous

Headline chips are inline-block runs on the headline's own baseline — inline-block, not inline-flex, because a flex box borrows its baseline from its first item, and that item is an icon tile with no baseline of its own, which would align the whole sentence to the bottom of the icon. Sized entirely in em, so tile and glyph track the clamp() without needing breakpoints of their own

The chip's icon tile follows the concentric-corner rule the frame and cards use — its radius is the chip's radius minus the chip's vertical padding — and is a plain round rect rather than a squircle, since a squircle nested two or three pixels inside a round rect reads as a different corner family

The CTAs are the project's shadcn Button with every bevel class passed at the call site; the background shorthand is marked important so the base component's `bg-clip-padding` cannot collapse the padding-box fill onto the border-box rim
Travelling pulses use pathLength={1}, so one dash length and one offset animation work on all three connectors no matter how far each runs, and keep working when the column resizes

The diagram is tinted with the frame's own greige rather than plain white — translucent tiles and cards over the photograph, connectors stroked in the same value — so the figure reads as belonging to the frame around it instead of sitting on the image

Dark theme covers the frame, panel, notch flares, chips and buttons; the photographic panel and the diagram over it are drawn once for both themes, since the diagram is light throughout and the photograph is fixed

Chip serif words read `var(--font-playfair, ui-serif, Georgia, serif)`. That variable is defined by the CraftUI app's own layout and by nothing else, so an installed copy resolves the fallback and sets the chips in Georgia — correct, just not the display face. Expose a Playfair Display, or any serif with a real italic, as `--font-playfair` on <html> to get the intended setting
Every entrance, the spinning hub rim and the pulses drop out under prefers-reduced-motion

sections.name: Navbar 01
sections.description: A flat top bar with divider-separated items. Hovering an item raises a solid accent strip out of the bottom rule until it fills the whole cell; the active route keeps a thin bar of the same shape. On phones the same strip turns on its side into a push-down accordion.

variations.name: default
variations.description: One strip, three states: hidden when idle, a thin bar on the active route, a full fill on hover. Width never changes, so the fill reads as the underline rising rather than a box appearing. Below md the items unroll inside the bar as rows and push the page down.

props.name: items
props.description: Nav entries, left to right. Defaults to Home / About / Services / Contact. The first item is also what the brand mark links to, and it starts as the active route.

props.name: className
props.description: Appended to the <nav> class list — where sticky positioning, a backdrop blur or a background colour go, since the bar itself ships transparent.

props.name: transition
props.description: Motion transition for the strip. Defaults to a spring (stiffness 440, damping 36, mass 0.4) so an interrupted hover reverses mid-flight instead of restarting.

props.name: labelDuration
props.description: Seconds the label colour takes to cross over once the fill arrives. Default 0.07.

props.name: labelDelay
props.description: Seconds the label waits before flipping to the on-fill colour. Applied on the way in only, so the ink clears before the strip retracts. Default 0.04.

props.name: accent
props.description: Fill colour of the strip — the hover fill and the active bar are the same shape, so this is both. Any CSS colour; defaults to a bright chartreuse.

props.name: labelColorOnFill
props.description: Label colour once the accent is behind it. Defaults to near-black — pick it against `accent`, not against the page. At rest the label is white.

props.name: barHeight
props.description: Height in pixels of the thin bar on the active route. Turned into a scaleY factor against the 64px bar, so nothing is measured at runtime. Default 3.

variations.previewHint: Hover the nav items — click one to move the active bar. Narrow the window for the mobile menu
features: One bottom-anchored strip covers every state — scaleY to 0, to a thin bar, or to 1 — so only a transform animates and it stays on the compositor
Both ends of the range are known numbers, so nothing is measured and the layout is never read during the hover
A single spring means an interrupted hover reverses mid-flight instead of blinking away, which a fade would do
Mobile runs the same cell rotated into a row: no hover exists on touch, so there the fill is the active state outright and the thin bar is dropped

The mobile panel pushes the page down instead of covering it — the one layout property animated here, on a tween rather than the item spring, since a spring's overshoot would bounce the content below it
Separators are inset box-shadows, not borders, so item widths stay exactly what the padding says — which is what the strip is sized from
Hover is only set for pointerType 'mouse', which sidesteps the sticky-hover-after-tap problem on touch, and the bar itself clears the hover on pointer leave
Focus mirrors hover, so keyboard tabbing fills the same strip, and reduced motion drops every animation to a zero-duration state change

sections.name: Feature Gallery 02
sections.description: A sticky scroll-driven gallery with a parallax image strip on the right and animated destination info on the left, connected by a flight-path arc divider.

variations.name: default
variations.description: Five travel destinations revealed through a sticky scroll. The right panel stacks images in a weighted parallax strip; the left panel slides in destination info driven by scroll position.
variations.previewHint: Scroll down to navigate through destinations
features: Lenis smooth scroll drives the entire layout via a single useScroll hook
Image strip uses scale + Y + rotate transforms so each image slots into a weighted parallax stack
Arc SVG divider renders a dashed flight path; a plane icon follows via offset-path and flips direction based on scroll velocity
Left panel text slots use AnimatePresence mode='wait' spring transitions — no layout shift
Stat values animate with useSpring so numbers count up smoothly on each destination change

sections.name: Feature Gallery 01
sections.description: A centered feature section — eyebrow, heading, subheading and a two-button CTA row — above a strip of image cards that expand on click. Written for a studio or portfolio site where the work needs to carry the section.

variations.name: default
variations.description: Cards rise into place on scroll, then the clicked card widens around a stationary image while the rest narrow. Heights never change; the label and scrim fade in last.

props.name: images
props.description: Cards in the strip. Each is { label, description?, src, tint } — description is an optional line rendered under the label on the expanded card, and tint is the solid colour shown behind the photo while it loads and in the collapsed sliver.

props.name: eyebrow
props.description: Small label above the heading, uppercased and letterspaced in CSS — pass it in natural case. Defaults to "What we do".

props.name: heading
props.description: Section heading, rendered as an h2. Accepts JSX, so individual words can be wrapped in a span to colour or style them — e.g. heading={<>Spaces designed around how you live}.

props.name: subheading
props.description: Supporting paragraph below the heading. Accepts JSX, so parts of the sentence can be emphasised with a span or a link.

props.name: ctaLabel
props.description: Primary button label. Defaults to "Book a consultation".

props.name: ctaHref
props.description: Primary button destination.

props.name: secondaryLabel
props.description: Secondary outline button label. Defaults to "View all projects".

props.name: secondaryHref
props.description: Secondary button destination.

props.name: defaultOpenIndex
props.description: Zero-based index of the card expanded when the section mounts. Defaults to 4 (the fifth card). Pass null for none; an index past the end of `images` is treated as null.

props.name: countNoun
props.description: Noun used in the "Showing 5 of 10 projects" line, which appears only if a breakpoint renders fewer cards than were passed. Defaults to "projects".

props.name: className
props.description: Additional classes on the section element.

variations.previewHint: Click any card to expand it; click it again to collapse. Arrow keys move across the strip
features: Each card carries an inset 1px hairline — pure black at 10% on light, pure white at 10% on dark — drawn as a top-most overlay rather than an inset box-shadow (which paints below the image) or an outline (which the card already spends on focus-visible), so a pale photo never bleeds into the page background
Entrance is staged, not one fade: the strip fades in at 120ms and cards rise from 10px, staggered 30ms apart
Opening a card animates width only — the photo is fixed at the expanded size and centred, so the card widens around a stationary image instead of rescaling it
Card heights are constant, so clicking never disturbs the strip's baseline or the surrounding layout
Collapsing runs in reverse order: scrim and caption leave together in 140ms on an ease-in, then geometry waits 150ms, so text is fully gone before a moving card edge can clip it

Opening stages four beats rather than one fade — scrim at 165ms, label at 225ms, description at 275ms, then a pair of corner crop marks at 310ms once the card has settled. Geometry, fades and exits each use their own easing curve

Corner brackets frame the open card, arced to the same radius as the card and shipped as the --gallery-frame token. They sit on the diagonal from 768px up, move to both top corners below that where the description wraps into the bottom-right, and mirror in RTL so they always stay clear of the caption
Card geometry switches across four breakpoints (34/40/48/54px collapsed). Below 768px the strip scrolls horizontally instead of dropping cards, so every image stays reachable on a phone

Arrow keys, Home and End move across the strip and open each card as they go; the opened card scrolls itself into view once it has finished widening. Each card reports aria-expanded rather than posing as a tab
Respects prefers-reduced-motion — the entrance and expand sequences resolve instantly to their end state

Card focus is a paired inset ring — a white band with a dark band outside it — drawn inside the card so it never overlaps a neighbour. The pairing is deliberate: a single white ring disappears on pale photography, which a gallery cannot predict

Scrim and label ship as --gallery-scrim and --gallery-label tokens. They stay white-on-dark in both themes by design: the label sits on a photograph, not on the page surface, so following the page theme would make it vanish in light mode.

sections.name: Feature AI 01
sections.description: A split feature section for AI, GPU and developer-infrastructure marketing pages: an isometric compute-stack diagram anchors the header, a list of capability words sits on the left, and an olive card on the right answers each one with body copy and a generative canvas loop. The card walks itself through all six capabilities on autoplay so a scroller sees the whole story, then hands control over permanently the moment someone hovers, focuses or taps a row. Useful anywhere a platform has more claims than a hero can hold and each claim needs its own sentence without stacking six cards down the page.

variations.name: default
variations.description: A split feature section for AI, GPU and developer-infrastructure marketing pages: an isometric compute-stack diagram anchors the header, a list of capability words sits on the left, and an olive card on the right answers each one with body copy and a generative canvas loop. The card walks itself through all six capabilities on autoplay so a scroller sees the whole story, then hands control over permanently the moment someone hovers, focuses or taps a row. Useful anywhere a platform has more claims than a hero can hold and each claim needs its own sentence without stacking six cards down the page.

props.name: capabilities
props.description: The rows in the list and the content of the card. Each is { word, art, copy } — word is the list label, copy is the card paragraph, and art is a loop from the exported FEATURE_AI_ART bundle (flow, pulse, columns, lorenzOrbit, dipole, lorenzSlice) or any custom { id, name, period, fps?, draw } of your own. Defaults to the exported DEFAULT_CAPABILITIES; an empty array falls back to it.

props.name: autoplayMs
props.description: Milliseconds each capability holds while the section is autoplaying. Defaults to 4000 — long enough to read the copy, short enough that a skimmer sees two or three before scrolling past.

props.name: className
props.description: Additional classes on the section element.

variations.previewHint: Wait and the card cycles on its own; hover or tap any capability to take over
features: Autoplays only while at least 35% of the section is in view and only until the first interaction, so the five capabilities nobody would have hovered still get read — and touch users, who have no hover at all, see the whole set
Hover previews the row while the pointer rests on it and a click commits it; the preview waits 100ms so sweeping the cursor down six rows fires one crossfade instead of six that cannot finish

Every card visual is a canvas loop drawn from a closed-form period — flow fields, gaussian pulse fronts, dipole fields and a numerically-found Lorenz periodic orbit whose residual drift is spread across the period so the seam is invisible
The canvas is inverted and composited with mix-blend-screen under a radial mask, so the olive gradient tints the marks and the art has no edge where the patch ends
Swaps are staggered art → label → copy, and exits run their own faster ease-in curve so a leaving element is gone before the next one arrives
The active-row marker is a shared layoutId dot, so it travels between rows instead of disappearing and reappearing
Card grain is a generated feTurbulence tile rather than a downloaded texture — no image request, and fractalNoise keeps it even instead of clumping
Inactive row ink is #6f6f6b rather than a pale grey, clearing the 3:1 large-text contrast floor on all six interactive rows
MotionConfig reducedMotion='user' collapses every spring and crossfade in the section, and the canvas loops freeze on their opening frame under prefers-reduced-motion

The isometric header diagram is computed entirely in world space through one projection function — no coordinate is placed by eye — and every solid is painted back to front so the stack occludes itself without z-index
shadcn Button, Card, Badge and Separator are restyled entirely at the call site through cn(), so the section drops into a project without touching the primitives

sections.name: Akta Hero 01
sections.description: A hero for data and API products drawn as a technical document rather than a marketing page: square planes separated by hairline rules, L-shaped corner crop marks as the only ornament, and an all-monospace UI voice. The panel at its centre demonstrates the product instead of describing it — a field of 168 ticks starts raw and denoises to the 197 signals that survive filtering, once, when it scrolls into view. Ships the full akta design language as prefixed tokens, so the same scale, devices and rules build every following section.

variations.name: default
variations.description: A hero for data and API products drawn as a technical document: square planes, hairline rules, corner crop marks, and an uppercase monospace UI voice against one blue accent. The centre panel denoises a 168-tick noise field down to its retained signals on scroll, the logo wall cycles customer wordmarks on a spring, and every token ships akta- prefixed so the design language is reusable across a whole site.

props.name: plateImage
props.description: Decorative photographic plate behind the panel cluster. Painted as a CSS background layer rather than an , so a missing file degrades to the hatch beneath it instead of a broken image. Pass null to force the hatch.

props.name: className
props.description: Additional classes on the section element.

variations.previewHint: Hover either CTA — the corner brackets pull flush and the label re-states itself. Scroll the panel into view to watch the noise field resolve into signal.
features: Borders are shadows: depth is a layered box-shadow and every separator is a single-edge inset shadow, so surfaces cost no layout space and stay transparent enough to survive on top of a photographic plate

The corner notch is one pseudo-element drawing a full border under a four-layer mask that keeps only the corners — no wrapper markup, no four spans, and the brackets track the element's real size at every breakpoint

Notch reveal animates `inset` rather than a transform, because pushing four corners outward needs a scale, and scale is proportional: on a 200x48 button that reads as ~8px sideways against ~2px vertically

The signal field rests filtered, not raw, so a no-JS or reduced-motion visitor meets the truthful end state rather than a field that never resolves; the raw state is only armed once motion is confirmed allowed
Tick heights come from a deterministic hash rather than Math.random(), so server and client render byte-identical markup instead of hydrating with a mismatch and a visible repaint
Rolling labels clip on the label wrapper, never the button — the button is a notch, and its brackets live outside the box, so overflow-hidden on it would shear them off
The logo wall gates its interval on in-view and stagger both the starting mark and the period by cell index, so six cells never flip in lockstep and nothing ticks off-screen

Full-bleed bands are siblings of the grid container, so their rules cross the whole viewport while the content stays on the 1440 rail; flush corner notches mark every junction where a rail meets a band
Every custom property, class and keyframe is akta- prefixed, so the block cannot collide with or be re-skinned by the host's own tokens
The palette is 22 literal oklch values rather than references to Tailwind's stops, so the block looks identical on Tailwind v3, v4, and in projects that customised their own blue
Respects prefers-reduced-motion throughout, and every resting state outside the motion guard is the meaningful one
